text.p: Stratosphere Corp, operator of the Stratosphere hotel and casino in Las Vegas, said Friday it is suspending construction on its new hotel tower.
An anticipated cash shortfall and its current debt restructuring talks led it to make the decision, Stratosphere said.
The company is 42-percent owned by Minneapolis-based Grand Casinos Inc.
Stratosphere's new tower was planned to have 1,000 new hotel room bays, a pool and spa and additional retail space.
The current property, which opened in April this year, has a 100,000 square foot casino, 1,500 hotel rooms, shopping and a centerpiece 1,149-foot tower with a restaurant at the top.
Stratosphere was building the new hotel tower to support the booming tourism in Las Vegas and draw more players into its casino.

But since opening in April, the casino has struggled with less traffic than the company originally anticipated. The result being that it reported a loss of $0.19 a share after analysts had expected it to produce a profit.
The company has since been hit with shareholder lawsuits, resignations and is working with bondholders to restructure its $203 million of outstanding first mortgage notes.
